newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 24.

-- POLLY THE CLONED LAMB MAY BE WORTH A MINT

Edinburgh-based PPL Therapeutics have created Polly, the first cloned transgenic sheep used to make human proteins from genes that can be used to treat people with protein deficiency. Other transgenic sheep have been created, such as Tracy in 1992, but cloning techniques mean that a whole flock of identical sheep can be created in one generation with present research allowing future sheep to be created to produce proteins to treat diseases ranging from haemophilia to osteoporosis. Polly-like produced proteins could be clinically tested as early as 1999. -- BRUSSELS AVERTS CRISIS BY AGREEING BOEING MERGER

EU competition commissioner Karel Van Miert announced that the plans for the Boeing-McDonnell Douglas merger have been approved following the final concessions of Boeing that will make licences and patents from McDonnell Douglas's defence research available to competition, with its civilian operations established separately from within Boeing and promises of no abuse of power over aircraft supplies sector influence. Van Miert called the dispute a vital battle to help settle terms of agreement.
-- SETTLEMENT HOPES RISE AS BA AND UNION TALK

The government conciliation service Acas held a meeting with BA managers and cabin crew union representatives of TGWU on how best to resolve the dispute over 42m stg cabin crew costs that sparked a three day strike at BA two weeks ago. Statements of progress are stalled until the talks have ended but debate still rages over the differing opinions of the TGWU branch Bassa and the smaller Cabin Crew 89 union which Bassa herald as a 'company union'.
-- SIB CLEARS WAY FOR ELECTRONIC TRADING

The Securities and Investments Board approved the final part of the plan to implement electronic trading at the London Stock Exchange so long as block share trading does not undermine the main market or else fresh initiatives would have to be implemented. The exchange is expected to announce by the end of July the implementation of a new order-driven market which is to supersede the original market-making system.
-- OFGAS AND BG ROW WORSENS

The gas watchdog authority Ofgas accused Transco of braking an agreement over how to deal in public with pipeline revenue calculations that could lead to Transco losing an additional 500m stg from its revenue following recommendations from the Monopolies and Mergers Commission. Ofgas regulator Ms Spottiswode said that the two sides had agreed to play down the change whilst BG declined to enter into argument over who said what.
-- LVMH LINK POSSIBLE THIS YEAR

Grand Metropolitan chief John McGrath has stated a merger between GrandMet, Guinness and France's LVMH will only occur if the benefits are divided fairly among shareholders of the three groups. LVMH, meanwhile has increased its stake in GrandMet from 6.4 per cent to 11.05 per cent and reduced its Guinness holding from 14.2 per cent to 12.46 per cent, meaning it is now capable of calling an emergency shareholder meeting.
-- CARLSBERG-TETLEY CUTS LIKELY

Britain's third largest brewer, Carlsberg-Tetley will initiate cost-cutting measures as a result of the blocking of its merger with Bass Breweries by trade and industry secretary Margaret Beckett. It is expected the company will end its brewing at Alloa in Scotland and possibly Wrexham in Wales along with the possible closure of 20 distribution depots. CT now holds a 14 per cent stake of the brewing market, compared with 28 per cent held by Scottish Courage and 23 per cent by Bass.
-- FORMULA ONE FLOTATION DATE UP IN THE AIR

Formula One Holding's founder and chief executive Bernie Ecclestone has increased the level of uncertainty surrounding the date of FOH's proposed flotation, as he stated on Wednesday, 'no decision has ever been made with respect to timing'. The statement was seen as an attempt to quiet speculation of the issue and concern over FOH's relations with US investment bank Salomon Brothers. A statement issued by the bank reveals flotation remains the 'preferred course' of FOH.
-- MATTHEW CLARK PUTS 8M STG BEHIND BRANDS

Cider and drinks wholesaler Matthew Clark announced it is to spend 8m stg on advertising its Blackthorn and Diamond White cider brands following a drop in pre-tax profit to 40.6m stg for the year ended 30/04/97 down from 70m stg for the same period last year. The advertising plan is part of a strategy to revitalise the firm's products after 5 per cent increases in cider prices would rule out a price war on the products that are still priced lower than two or three years ago.
-- PACE SHARES TAKE FRESH BACKWARDS STEP

Pace Micro Technology reported that pre-tax profit held at 18.4m stg for the year ended 31/05/97 although turnover rose 12 per cent to 219.6m stg, the discrepancy being partly due to a 45 per cent increase in overheads to 38m stg. Pace shares dropped 15 per cent in one day to 53.5p following the annual report but the cable and satellite TV receiver and decoder manufacturer blamed uncertainty in its main markets on ongoing changes in the broadcast sector.
